question: Check count-only evidence coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy across PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, DailyMed, LactMed and MPRINT. Explain what each count does and does not establish.
criteria: Use count-only probes. LactMed is lactation-only and not applicable to pregnancy. Do not equate counts or zero matches with evidence quality or safety. Preserve unknown versus zero.
answer:
## Count-only evidence coverage for daridorexant in pregnancy

| Source | Count | What the count does establish | What it does not establish |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **PubMed** [S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) | **3** | Three records matched the returned daridorexant-and-pregnancy search. | The records may not represent distinct studies, human pregnancy evidence, or reports with relevant outcomes. The count does not establish study quality, findings, or safety. The returned search also did not find the daridorexant MeSH-term phrase. |
| **ClinicalTrials.gov** [S1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/) | **4** | Four registration records matched the returned query. | The count does not establish enrollment, current status, posted results, outcomes, or confirmed pregnancy applicability. Population details and study relevance were not reviewed in this count-only lookup. |
| **DailyMed** [S2](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/) | **1** | One name-matched product-label record was found. | It does not establish that the label contains pregnancy-specific evidence, that the product is the intended formulation, or that the information represents independent clinical evidence. The product and relevant label sections were not reviewed here. |
| **LactMed** [S6](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/) | **Not applicable** | No pregnancy count was generated because LactMed is a lactation-only resource. | LactMed cannot establish pregnancy evidence or serve as general pediatric evidence. |
| **MPRINT Gold snapshot** [S3](https://github.com/langli-lab/mprint-kp-data) | **0 literal-name rows; 0 distinct PMIDs** | No literal daridorexant match was found in the selected MPRINT Gold snapshot tables. Snapshot date: **2026-11-17**. | This is not proof that no relevant publication exists, no evidence exists elsewhere, or daridorexant is safe in pregnancy. The returned MPRINT count reflects literal-name matching in selected snapshot tables, without name resolution or a full-portal search; rows are not necessarily distinct studies. This was a **Gold snapshot** lookup, not a Silver classification lookup. |

The counts are **not comparable across sources** and represent presence/navigation metadata only. Full records, study populations, article findings, label content, and registry statuses were not retrieved, so the review cannot determine what the records found or assess clinical safety. The returned pregnancy band was not confirmed against each source’s actual population, gestational age, or prematurity details.

The MPRINT snapshot’s zero is specifically “no match returned by this query/snapshot,” not proof of absence elsewhere. Similarly, the PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and DailyMed counts do not establish that the matched records contain pregnancy-specific evidence.

The lookup also reported that no curated federal pregnancy counterpart to LactMed was identified in its prototype source review; this is a limitation of that MCP review, not proof that no such resource exists. [S5](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/labeling/questions-and-answers-pregnancy-and-lactation-labeling-rule) [S6](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501922/)
